mentioned.quote: Without any safeguards, we recognize that advanced AI models could lower the barrier to entry for bad actors seeking to develop chemical, biological, radiological, or nuclear (“CBRN”) or cyber weapons

threshold.quote: In this RMF, we particularly focus on requests that pose a foreseeable and non-trivial risk of more than one hundred deaths or over $1 billion in damages from weapons of mass destruction or cyberterrorist attacks on critical infrastructure
threshold.note: Ambiguous: request-level risk criterion (deaths or dollars) that triggers heightened safeguards (p.2-3); counted as a quantitative domain criterion.

response.note: p.2 'apply heightened safeguards' names none; p.5 'xAI currently relies on our basic refusal policy to prevent misuse for cyber attacks' and 'still working on identifying enforceable critical steps' are practice and unfinished work; p.6 input and output filters are unconditional practice (E1); the p.5 acceptance criterion covers biology and chemistry only.

acc_decider.note: Only 'we integrate the approach of designating risk owners, including assigning responsibility for proactively mitigating identified risks' (p.8); no named role or body decides whether a threshold is reached or whether to deploy.

acc_external.note: External involvement is not committed: p.1-2 'works with a variety of governmental bodies ... private testing firms' describes bottleneck identification; p.4 independent third-party assessments are past findings; p.7-8 'we may also provide vetted and qualified external red teams ... unredacted versions' is hedged.

acc_unmet.note: No statement of what happens if a required response is unmet; p.9 shutdown steps are all 'may' and cover imminent catastrophic events; p.8 employee reporting of nonadherence goes to no named body.
